result.title: Phantom Success, Silent Failure: Auditing the Success Checkers of Simulated Manipulation Benchmarks
result.summary: Simulated manipulation benchmarks measure policy performance using hand-written success checkers that label each episode as a success or failure. Passing an expert demonstration shows that a checker accepts one way of completing the task. Learned policies, however, may stop after partial progress or complete the task in a different way. A checker may then accept an incomplete execution (phantom success) or reject an execution that satisfies the instruction (silent failure). In this paper, we introduce SimAudit, an LLM-based pipeline that audits success checkers against task instructions. SimAudit analyzes the instruction and checker code to identify scenarios where the two may disagree, recreates those scenarios in simulation, and runs the original checker. Multi-view renderings are then used to verify whether the observed behavior satisfies the instruction. Across RoboTwin 2.0, RoboCasa365, and RoboDojo, 183 simulated test cases produced the predicted checker verdict. Visual verification and deduplication yielded 61 distinct defects across 49 tasks, including 40 phantom successes and 21 silent failures. Most defects in RoboCasa365 accepted incomplete executions, most in RoboDojo rejected valid executions, and both error types were common in RoboTwin 2.0. These findings suggest that validating success checkers requires testing both incomplete executions and valid alternatives to expert demonstrations, and motivate more rigorous evaluation protocols for future benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SimAudit，用 LLM 分析任务指令与 success checker 代码，找出二者可能判断不一致的情形，在仿真中复现并用多视角渲染核验行为是否真正满足指令，审计 RoboTwin 2.0 等三个平台的判定器，共报告 61 处缺陷，区分出 phantom success 与 silent failure 两类错误。
AI.relevance_reason: 「判定标准与实际行为不符」的诊断形式及多视角视觉核验，可能可供核查 LVR 中成功判定是否真正依据视觉证据、以及如何构造模糊情形来检验验证协议；但该文不涉及 latent 推理状态，联系较为间接。
